findings: START CONTENTION: pgrep -c headless_shell = 14, loadavg 11.81 -> above the 8 cap. Authoring phase first, no browser. git working tree CLEAN at start; W1-04, W1-FACTIONS, W1-ATTR-SCALE all report state=complete, so the NPC and quest files are not being written under me right now.

THE TREE HAS MOVED SINCE THE VERDICT. 120 quests now (was 94): side 25, faction 62, hidden 1, main 32. All 120 name a giver. 39 UNIQUE giver ids, and ALL 39 HAVE AN NPC RECORD. So the defect is not missing records — it is that a record is not a spawn.

WHY THE WORLD IS EMPTY, exactly. Engine.applyNamedState() spawns ONLY `patch.npcs` from the state file. helstrom-market declares 4, stormhold-street 3, soulrest-quay 5, thorn-hall 0 -> the twelve. W1-04 built Engine.populateSettlement(sid), which spawns everyone whose record names that town, and sim/settlement.js:161 calls it — but ONLY on a settlement CROSSING (`if (want !== sim.env.settlement)`). No bootable state stands the player inside a settlement radius, and applyNamedState never calls populate at all. So the mechanism to fill a town exists and is never reached from a state load. critic-giver-presence.mjs calls loadState then listNPCs with NO steps, so even the crossing path could not fire.

STATE ENV AUDIT: of the four town states only soulrest-quay declares env.settlement. helstrom-market/stormhold-street declare env.interior = 'helstrom-market'/'stormhold-street', which are NOT real interiors (game/data/world/interiors/ has 115 and neither is among them). thorn-hall and writ-house and barge-hold ARE real interiors.

GIVER SETTLEMENTS (39 unique): gideon 7, helstrom 5, soulrest 4, blackrose 4, thorn 4, stormhold 3, archon 3, lilmoth 3, tidewrack 1, null 5. Only 4 of the 8 settlements have any bootable state, so half the givers had nowhere to be placed even if populate ran.

THE 5 NULL-SETTLEMENT GIVERS ARE NOT A DATA ERROR. speaker-teel-ashaan (5 quests) and xul-aneekh-speaker (3) are declared at 'the hollow, a day east of Helstrom on the root track'; ixtu-meer (3) 'Under the Stone Wastes, the counting chamber'; keeper-teeja-lun (1) 'The Bone Ladder, the sapwell under the rib'. These are wilderness/dungeon givers and W1-04's rule (settlement:null is correct for someone who belongs to no town) applies. Only potter-mek is a genuine miss — one of its two quests is located at gideon-lowmarket, where fence-ashul already stands.

talkTo() HAS NO DISTANCE TERM AND NO CELL TERM — it only requires sim.findNPC(eid). So the critic's `talkable` is, today, exactly `in sim.npcs`. listNPCs() likewise returns every entity, visible or not.

PRESENCE IS ALREADY MODELLED, and well: sim/npc.js stepSchedule() sets n.at from the schedule slot for the hour and n.present/n.visible from `n.at === null || n.at === sim.env.interior`. So spawning a whole town is safe — people in other cells are invisible. The `at === null => present everywhere` branch is what an outdoor person needs fixing for.

populateSettlement() PLACES PEOPLE IN THE WRONG SPACE for an exterior: positions are derived from the interior's bounds around the ORIGIN, and settlements stand at world coordinates (helstrom [2262.5,27.22,2773.5]). It also reads schedule[0].at rather than the slot for the current hour.

utility-findability.mjs --state CRASH CONFIRMED at line 51: `(args.state ? String(args.state).split(',') : '<defaults>').split(',')` — the ternary yields an ARRAY when --state is given and .split is then called on it.
mainline-chain-floor.mjs:198 conjures the giver: `H.spawnNPC({ from_record: giver, pos: [0,0,2] })`, guarded only by the standing-refusal branch.

TWO ROOT CAUSES IN populateSettlement(), both found by reading rather than measuring, both now fixed. (1) it read schedule[0].at — the FIRST row of the day whatever the hour — so a person whose midnight slot is their house was placed in their house at noon. (2) it derived every position from an INTERIOR's bounds_m, a cell-local frame centred on nothing, and settlements stand at world coordinates (helstrom [2262.5,27.22,2773.5]) — so it would have heaped every town's people around the world origin, kilometres from the town.

EVERY PRE-EXISTING TOWN STATE IS A SCENE AT THE WORLD ORIGIN. soulrest-quay declares settlement:soulrest and stands the player at [0,0,-4]; Soulrest is at [610.5,7.91,4877]. That is why four state files could hold twelve people between them: a hand-placed scene is exactly as populated as somebody remembered to type. The 8 new town-<id> states stand at the town's own coordinates and declare nobody by hand.

presenceMode has THREE settings deliberately — on | report | off. `report` exists so the term can be measured against the whole tree before it is allowed to refuse anything; the dispatch's warning that landing it fail-closed early has taken the engine down four times is the reason it is a field and not an if.
CONTENTION during the build phase: headless_shell went 14 -> 12 -> 30 and loadavg 11.8 -> 9.6 -> 19.35. Browser phase deferred; all of the above is authoring done with no browser open.

HEADLINE, MEASURED: critic-giver-presence.mjs (unmodified questions, derived state list) reports quests_with_a_giver 120, giver_present_in_some_state 120, giver_talkable_in_some_state 120. By category: main 32/32, side 25/25, faction 62/62, hidden 1/1. Verdict acceptance was >=60/94 with side >=20/25. Was 9/94 with side 0/25 and faction 0/36.

Per state, NPCs in the world: town-gideon 41 (26 giver-quests), town-helstrom 58 (17), town-lilmoth 50 (10), town-soulrest 29 (15), town-stormhold 49 (9), town-thorn 23 (11), town-archon/blackrose likewise. helstrom-market went 4 -> 58 and thorn-hall 0 -> 23 with NO edit to their `npcs:` blocks — only `env.settlement` and the populate call.

A NEW STATE FILE IS NOT IN THE BUILD UNTIL game/data/index.json IS REGENERATED. loadState threw `no such named state` for all ten new states until `node tools/analysis/data-index.mjs` was run (525 -> 538 files). Worth knowing: check-data passes on a stale index because the index and the tree were consistent; it is the ADDITION that is invisible.

THE ORIGINAL --sabotage assume-present CONTROL IS NOW VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION and must not be cited as proof: it worked in the verdict because presence went 9 -> 94 while talkable stayed 9. With the world populated both are 120, so the two runs agree. The falsifying control has to be DELETE-THE-FIX on the population instead.

SIDE ITEM CLOSED, and it corrects the count: of W1-04's `9 NPC topic ids with no body`, only SIX are real. `the chapter's vote`, `the interior's consent` and `the ledger's terms` resolve fine — game/src/core/topics.js#topicKey folds an apostrophe INTO the word (`the chapters vote`) and 50-mainline.json carries all three as `the-chapters-vote`/`the-interiors-consent`/`the-ledgers-terms`. The audit used its own slug, which split on the apostrophe. An audit that does not use the runtime's own key function reports gaps the runtime does not have.

SIDE ITEM CLOSED: the six real ones are all on writ-house.json — the opening cell, the two people you meet before you have a name — and are now authored in game/data/dialogue/topics/56-writ-house-open.json (the-hold, your-hatch-name, the-writ, my-work, the-list, lukiul), 4 filtered infos each with race requires/forbids and a disposition band, last row ungated. Missing-topic count is now 0 measured with the real topicKey.
SIDE ITEM CLOSED: VP04-settlement-street repointed from `settlement_primary_street` (camera hardcoded at [4,1.7,-6], the world origin) to `town-thorn` with the camera at Thorn's own coordinates.

LIKE-FOR-LIKE, on the EXACT four states the critic tool shipped with (--legacy-states, no new state file counted): giver_talkable_in_some_state 9 -> 52 of 120. main 9 -> 19, side 0 -> 14, faction 0 -> 19, and 0 -> 4 helstrom-market NPCs became 58, thorn-hall 0 -> 23. So the number moves without any of the eight new town states being in the sum.

DELETE-THE-FIX, and it lands on the verdict's own figure to the digit. Removing ONE call — `this.populateSettlement(sid)` in applyNamedState — and re-running --legacy-states gives talkable 9/120, main 9, side 0, faction 0. That is exactly the 9 / 0 / 0 the W1-19 round-2 verdict measured. Restored immediately afterwards; engine.js re-checked.

CONSUMPTION, 5/5, and the self-test is a real breakage rather than an inverted assertion: tools/quests/w1-giver-presence-consumption.mjs. C1 the same quest and gate refuse for absence in arena_flat and not in town-soulrest; C2 disarming the term in the same world stops the refusal; C3 with the term armed and the giver there the quest is NOT refused for absence (so it is not a rubber stamp); C4 talkTo opens a conversation in the town and throws where nobody is; C5 the town state's `npcs:` block is EMPTY and the world has 29 people in it. --self-test performs BREAK-TERM (pin the gate off) and BREAK-WORLD (boot the empty state as the town) and 5/5 go red under the breakage that should kill them.

MY OWN FIRST SELF-TEST WAS WORTHLESS and is recorded rather than quietly fixed: it inverted the ASSERTION instead of breaking the MECHANISM, so it reported STILL-GREEN five times and proved nothing. AGENT-PROTOCOL failure mode 2, in my own instrument, on the first try.

utility-findability, on its three ORIGINAL default states, now reports 7 quests opened by playing (was 10) — and all 7 have a giver standing in the town, where 0 of the 10 did. The three that fell away were quests the gate would have offered with nobody to say the words to; they now show under `blocked NO GIVER HERE` (helstrom 31, stormhold 31, soulrest 34), which is the honest answer for a per-town measurement: you have to travel.

--state NOW WORKS and thorn-hall was measured for the first time: 4 towns (town-helstrom, town-gideon, town-thorn, thorn-hall) give 23 quests opened by playing, all with the giver present. Thorn alone goes 2 cold -> 7 after, learning 12 quest keywords.

mainline-chain-floor with the conjuring removed and the presence term ARMED still reports 40/40 signatures completing both chains, 0/31 gates arriving short, 0 bought, 0 violent — and 0 giver_absent entries. The chain is now walked against real people rather than against bodies the probe made up.

RED CONTROL MIS-AIMED FIRST TIME, recorded rather than hidden: stripping undersexton-aveline-rell's settlement/post did NOT make the chain-floor go red, because soulrest-quay's `npcs:` block HAND-PLACES her. That is itself the shape of the original defect — the one giver who was always in the world was the one somebody had typed into a state file. Re-aimed at neeja-xul (Q-MAIN-07/14/19/29), who is hand-placed in no state.

THE BOX BROKE UNDER ME MID-RUN, and it was not mine: `ReferenceError: ImpactAudio is not defined at engine.js:290` on a fresh boot, while `import { ImpactAudio } from './audio/impact-audio.js'` is present on line 40. Another agent was mid-write on game/src/engine.js and game/src/world/field.js (W1-PROSE-R2 status file moving at the same time). boot-check PASSes again afterwards. If you see this error, re-run before believing it.
